Checking for absence of //form[@id='webauth'] via findElement + broad Exception catch is brittle. Use Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...) or findElements(...).isEmpty() so the assertion is explicit and doesn't mask other exceptions

UsernameForm calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() without arguments, but the only available method is isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) in UsernamePasswordForm. This won't compile. Update the call to pass the appropriate user or add a no-arg overload that delegates appropriately

isConditionalPasskeysEnabled currently requires user != null, which prevents WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.fillContextForm() from running on the initial login page (where context.getUser() is typically null). That means enableWebAuthnConditionalUI/challenge/rpId won't be set and the passkeys conditional UI form won't be rendered. Consider removing the user != null requirement or splitting the logic
Unused import: PasswordCredentialModel is imported but not referenced anywhere in this test class. Please remove it to keep the test compiling cleanly under strict build/checkstyle settings

The test asserts that the WebAuthn form is not present by calling driver.findElement(...) and catching a broad Exception. Since findElement never returns null (it throws when missing), this pattern is brittle and can hide unrelated failures. Prefer Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...) or use findElements(...).isEmpty() to check absence explicitly
This method overrides WebAuthnAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators; it is advisable to add an Override annotation
